about.title: Calistoga Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When someone dies because another person or business was careless, California gives certain family members a way to hold that party accountable in civil court. Calistoga is home to about 5,330 people at the north end of Napa County, and a loss here is felt widely. Public records show 13 injury collisions and 16 people hurt in 2025 and no traffic deaths that year, with most activity along Rt 29, Foothill Boulevard, Rt 128 and Lincoln Avenue. Wrongful death claims, though, reach beyond the roadway. A fall at a spa or lodging property, an error in medical care, a defective product, or an incident at a job site can all give rise to a claim. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects grieving families with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there is a recovery. State law allows two years from the date of death, less when a public agency is involved, so it helps to reach out early.

whyChoose.title: What Calistoga Families Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Who is allowed to bring the claim
items.desc: California limits standing to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can confirm which family members qualify before anything is filed.

items.title: The deadline is firm and sometimes short
items.desc: Families generally have two years from the date of death to file. If a city, county, or state agency may share responsibility, the window to act is considerably shorter.

items.title: Real losses, honestly accounted for
items.desc: Recoverable damages can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. This is a civil matter that proceeds separately from any criminal case.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on Rt 29 or Rt 128 near Calistoga. Does it matter who maintains the road?
items.answer: It can. If the design or upkeep of a state highway or county road played a part, a claim against that public agency follows a much shorter deadline than the standard two years. An attorney can sort out whether a driver, a company, or an agency may be responsible and protect each deadline.

items.question: Can more than one relative file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Eligible family members typically join a single action rather than filing separately. Spouses, domestic partners, and children come first under state law, followed by certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can help the family bring one coordinated claim.

items.question: Do we have to wait for a criminal case to finish before pursuing a civil claim?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death action is a civil case and moves on its own track, regardless of whether charges are filed or how a criminal case ends. Waiting can also eat into the two-year filing period, so it is wise to speak with an attorney early.
